summary:
# NOTES ON THE THREE BOOKS (for detailed Q&A)

## BOOK 1 — "The Fatal Three" (Braddon, M. E.), Vol. I (Gutenberg 75410). Book the First: "Clotho; or Spinning the Thread."

**Ch I "We have been so happy."** Mr. John Fausset (stout, middle-aged, ex-wholesale silk firm, Lyons/St. Paul's Churchyard) and wife Maud Fausset (née Donfrey, 3rd dau. of Lord Castle-Connell, Irish peer, 19 at marriage, 9 yrs married). Daughter Mildred (7, golden hair, doll, "wax and bran"). House: Upper Parchment Street, off Grosvenor Sq./Park Lane. Fausset wants to adopt orphan girl Fay (13–14), his ward, heiress, sole trustee; "distant relation." Maud objects ("golden circle of home-life"). Mildred pleads "Let the little girl come, mother." Fausset: "Wisdom has spoken." Mildred offers her Paris walking doll.

**Ch II "Fay."** Next afternoon: Fay (tall, thin, olive complexion, big black eyes, badly dressed) arrives from Streatham Common school in hansom; Fausset's trunk in four-wheeler. Maud calls her "plain"; Fay says "I hate lessons"; loves books. Mildred hugs Fay; "You darling, how I shall adore you!" Fay put in Bell's room (servant Bell objects). Fay refused doll. Sisters' room dispute. Maud: "owl in an ivy-bush."

**Ch III "A Superior Person."** Mildred loves Fay; Maud jealous. Bell (Martha Bell, 48, ex-wet nurse of Maud at Castle-Connell, husband Patrick Bell died in Canada, iron-gray hair, no cap, black silk) rules household, hates Fay. Fay's disputes with Bell; Bell's "I'm sure I shouldn't like..." Fausset shouts.

**Ch IV "All she could remember."** Fay's memories: childhood in cottage on windy hill by sea, nurse "Nounou", a column with statue, French-speaking; then strange old lady, then school (Miss Constable, Streatham, Fay expelled after temper outburst). Fay's 'I hate everybody in this house.' The Hook (riverside villa, Chertsey–Windsor). Mildred scarlet fever; Fay nurses her. Bell and Meta (German maid) gossip overheard by Mildred: Fay is Fausset's daughter. Mildred asks to call Fay "sister"; Maud angry; Fay: "I hate everybody else in this house." Fay sent to Eastover-like Eastbourne? (no—Fay sent away to Brussels finishing school, Mildred returns to find her gone).

**Ch V "Without the Wolf."** Greswold family, Enderby Manor (Hampshire, near Romsey, New Forest). George Greswold, wife Mildred (née Fausset, now ~31), daughter Lola (12, golden hair, blue eyes, angelic). Village fever; Lola carried milk to sick cottagers ("Red Riding Hood, only without the wolf"). Dr. Porter (village doctor). Dr. Hutchinson (Southampton). Polly Rainbow (flaxen child, carries milk). Mrs. Wadman (dairy woman) used polluted garden well water for dairy. Greswold sacks Wadman/bailiff Thomas. Greswold: "Judgment." Dairy with Minton tiles. Lola's study "There shall be no suggestion of school".

**Ch VI "Ah! Pity! The lily is withered."** Polly dies; Lola falls ill (typhoid); Scotland trip cancelled; Lola dies after ~10 days; bell tolls; funeral. Greswold: "She was the morning." Lola's grave: "Laura, the only child of George and Mildred Greswold, aged twelve." Widow Rainbow: "She was all I had."

**Ch VII "Drifting apart."** Lake Thun villa. Greswold's "bad dream": "The cage—the cage again—iron bars—like a wild beast!" Mildred's Fay memories; Maud's death (heart disease) ~ 2 years after; deathbed: Fay was Fausset's natural daughter, mother "low common woman." Maud's disapproval. Fausset, Mildred go to Europe; Fausset dies of pneumonia in Parchment Street (~ 1 yr later, Oct, Mildred 16–17 hers); Mildred's Hook summers; Fausset's letters.

**Ch VIII "Such things were."** Greswold met Mildred at The Hook: Greswold (son of George Ransome of Magdalen, Oxford; younger son; mother left him Enderby). Mildred ~17, Greswold 13 years older. He changes name to Greswold. Return to Enderby; "clean sweep" of servants; Bell remains. Greswold at grave: "Judgment! judgment!"

**Ch IX "The face in the church."** Summer; Pamela Ransome (niece, Randolph's daughter, flaxen, plump, sister Rosalind married Sir Henry Mountford, Rainham Hall) invited. Dog Box (fox-terrier). Mildred sees auburn-bearded man Castellani in church ("Judas face"). Greswold's Rapport w/ Kassandra (Irish setter). Rollinson curate.

**Ch X "There is always the skeleton."** Riverdale (Hillersdon estate; Louise Hillersdon née Lorraine, ex-adventuress). César Castellani calls, claims author of *Nepenthe*; says Greswold lived in Nice with first wife. Greswold's guilty reaction; first wife's identity hidden.

**Ch XI "The beginning of doubt."** Greswold: first marriage "a sad remembrance"; Mildred's fear of divorced wife. Pamela's Agnosticism; Castellani. Mildred's jealous reverie.

**Ch XII "She cannot be unworthy."** Castellani visit; invites Cancellor and Louise Hillersdon to tea. Clement Cancellor (Vicar, St. Elizabeth's Parchment Street, Mildred's old tutor). Mildred: "If Mr. Cancellor likes her she cannot be unworthy."

**Ch XIII "Shall she be less than another?"** Cancellor's background; Louise's "repentance." Tea party. Deceased Wife's Sister's Bill debate; Greswold defends; Cancellor furious. Castellani's Wedding March; Heine songs. Concert plan (Rollinson, Burne-Jones window fund). Pamela smitten; Mildred warns Pamela.

**Ch XIV "Lifting the curtain."** Concert preparations; Castellani at Enderby daily. Mildred's question: first wife's death "infinitely sad." Confrontation in library: Greswold's first wife's photograph (Vivien Faux) — Mildred faints.

## BOOK 1 notes continued
Ch I–XIV is Vol I (ends with Mildred fainting). Vol I ends "END OF VOL. I."

## BOOK 2 — "The Fatal Three," Vol. II. Book the Second: "Lachesis; or the Meter of Destiny."

**Ch I "A wife and no wife."** Castellani's reputation (Magnus Dudley, claims he's Cavour's natural son or Milanese musician's son). Concert day: Mildred ill; concert success; Rollinson. Mildred leaves Enderby at 7 pm via Ivy Cottage (Miss Fisher's) to Waterloo; Greswold waits at station. Mildred's letter: Fay was her sister; their marriage unlawful. Greswold: "Pamela" asked to stay.

**Ch II "The sins of the fathers."** Greswold's inquiry with servant Bell: suspected Fausset was Fay's father; Greswold concludes possible sisterhood; Bell's story.

**Ch III "The verdict of her church."** Mildred at Mrs. Tomkison's (Cecilia Tomkison, husband Adam) in Queen Anne's Gate; Cancellor advises Mildred that marriage is incestuous; Greswold's letter. Mildred's reply.

**Ch IV "No light."** Miss Gertrude Fausset (aunt) in Lewes Crescent, Brighton, 57, St. Edmund's Church. Aunt advises return to husband; Mildred learns aunt's past (Milan, love affair with Paolo Castellani, sham marriage, daughter Fay). Castellani present at Lewes Crescent with Pamela.

**Ch V "The future might be darker."** Greswold visits Pergament & Pergament (Lincoln's Inn Fields); Vivien Faux's trust. Greswold and Mildred part. Miss Fausset's Maltravers (Vicar, St. Edmund's).

**Ch VI "Higher views."** Mildred sick; Brighton; Pamela's romance with Castellani; Maltravers wants transept; Mildred at Pallanza; Castellani pursuit.

**Ch VII "The time has come."** Pallanza; Castellani's proposal refused; Mildred's rejection: "You are a murderer" accusation (Castellani hints Greswold murdered first wife).

**Ch VIII "Not proven."** Nice: Lady Lochinvar (Palais Montano) reveals first wife Vivien Ransome died in April 1868, pushed/fell from cliff at St. Jean; George Ransome accused, imprisoned, then in asylum at Nice (St. André). Mildred visits Dr. Leroy.

**Ch IX "Looking back."** Mildred at Villa Montfleuri (Le Bout du Monde) in St. Jean; flower-woman; asylum visit; Maria Castellani (opera singer, Paolo's cousin). Pamela engaged to Malcolm Stuart (Lady Lochinvar's nephew, Scots).

## BOOK 3 — "The Fatal Three," Vol. III (Book the Third: "Atropos; or That Which Must Be").

Actually the Braddon text ends Vol. II in Ch IX. Vol. III continues: Ch I "A Wrecked Life" (Dr. Leroy and Maria Castellani; Pamela–Stuart). Ch II "In the Morning of Life" (Greswold's background; Ransome's youth; marriage to Vivien Faux in Florence). Ch III "Rift in the Lute" (Viva's jealousy; cliff; Ransome pushes wife? Viva throws herself off cliff; Ransome arrested). Ch IV "Darkness" (Ransome's imprisonment, madness, Venusian/Daan? no—mental illness). Ch V "The Grave on the Hill" (Mildred visits Fay's grave, rose cross). Ch VI "Pamela changes her mind" (Castellani at Nice; Pamela breaks with him; engaged to Stuart). Ch VII "As the sands run down" (Mildred returns to Brighton; Miss Fausset ill; Rollinson's letter says Greswold "heart broken"). Ch VIII "How should I greet thee?" (Mildred at Enderby grave, Greswold: "What brings you here"; Mildred at Mason's cottage; Brighton; Pamela to marry Stuart; Honeymoon at The Hook). Ch IX "Litera scripta manet" (Mildred finds letters in father's bookcase at The Hook: Fay's birth from Fausset with Fanny/Vivien Faux; Fausset's secret deed of gift £30,000; Mildred's note to Miss Fausset). Ch X "Marked by Fate" (Mildred returns to Enderby; reconciliation; heart weak; doctor Porter; physician Jenner/Clark advice). Ch XI "Like a Tale That is Told" (Pamela's wedding in Westminster Abbey; Miss Fausset dies early winter, leaves fortune to Mildred; Greswold Hospital founded; Castellani's later decline; "THE END").

NOTE on book structure: the source text contains Vol. I (Books "Clotho," Chs I–XIV), Vol. II (Book "Lachesis," Chs I–IX), and Vol. III ("Atropos," Chs I–XI).

## BOOK 2 (Guy Boothby: "A Bid for Fortune; or, Dr. Nikola's Vendetta") — separate text

Prologue (Dr. Nikola): Manager Mr. McPherson and bookkeeper Miss O'Sullivan, Imperial Restaurant, Thames Embankment. Letter from Cuyaba, Brazil, orders dinner for 4 in Room 22. Guests: Eastover (Best Dressed, American accent, from Nashville/Tahupapa/Papeete/Pekin), Prendergast (white-haired, pitted with smallpox), Baxter (clerical, undersized, bow-legged). Nikola: black cat, dark olive skin, black hair, thirty-three. Plans: Eastover to Sydney; Prendergast to Paris/Charing Cross; Baxter to tutor Lord Beckenham (Duke of Glenbarth's son), Bournemouth. Payment £10,000 each. Target: "Wetherell" (photograph). Ends: "The Green Sailor" public-house, East India Dock Road.

**Ch I "I determine to take a holiday."** Narrator Richard (Dick) Hatteras, 28, Thursday Island pearler, 6'2", father James Dymoke Hatteras (English, lost at sea). Sydney: Dorunda Dodson swindler; rescues Phyllis Wetherell (daughter of Colonial Secretary Sylvester Wetherell, Potts Point) from larrikins in Domain. Ship *Orizaba*; Phyllis confesses love at Naples; father forbids.

**Ch II "London."** Letters from Phyllis; restaurant chess man = Nikola; cards reveal names; scrying-dish vision of Phyllis crying. Phyllis and father left London for Paris suddenly.

**Ch III "I visit my relations."** Father's family at Murdlestone, Hampshire (New Forest). Uncle Sir William Hatteras (miserly), daughter Gwendoline (deformed). Hatteras refuses £1000; Catullus book.

**Ch IV "I save an important life."** Yacht *Enchantress* (Bournemouth); rescues Lord Beckenham (Marquis) from drowning; Baxter tutor.

**Ch V "Mystery."** Duke of Glenbarth visits; Baxter telegram "Nineveh" to Nikola; Baxter's Andaman evasion; Dick sends fake telegram.

**Ch VI "I meet Dr. Nikola again."** Meeting with Percival (ship *Yarraman*); Green Sailor pub; Baxter & Nikola; Nikola hypnotises; West of England express; Dick drugged, awakes Plymouth.

**Ch VII "Port Said."** Ship *Saratoga*; Beckenham sea-sick (drugged by Baxter); they visit Port Said mosque; arrested by Prendergast/men.

**Ch VIII "Our imprisonment and attempt at escape."** Iron collars, cell; mice carry messages; file; escape.

**Ch IX "Dr. Nikola permits us a free passage."** Nikola's room of curiosities; blindfolded release; Agent (Baxter) denies; they catch *Pescadore* to Melbourne.

**Part II Ch I "We reach Australia."** Sydney, *General Officer Hotel*, Palgrave Street. Phyllis reveals a suitor; Wetherell angry. Beckenham kidnapped (substitute "Marquis" at Government House). Coachman Thompson drugged at *Canary Bird*. Ponson St/Calliope St (Venneage). Beckenham found bound at 22 Calliope St.

**Ch II "On the trail."** Beckenham's story: Mathew Draper; Nikola; Eastover; drugged. Hatteras finds Draper's house 83 Charlemagne St.; Goddard & James curio hire; Dawson & Gladman (Hatteras inherits baronetcy: Sir Richard Hatteras, Murdlestone; cousin Gwendoline dead).

**Ch III "Lord Beckenham's story"** and follow-up with envelope from "The Man Who Knows" demanding £100,000 (ransom via China Pete's little stick). Footman James. Maid Sally. Fake ransom bags; police boat; *Maid of the Mist*.

**Ch IV "Following up a clue."** Wetherell's "stick" (China Pete's Chinese talisman); Hatteras's chase of maid to Sally's house in Sydney's low quarter; Phyllis taken to island Pipa Lannu via McMurtough's yacht.

**Ch V "The islands."** Voyage; Wetherell's story of China Pete, Nikola's attempts to buy the stick; island raid; Phyllis rescued; Beth-less; Phyllis tells capture (Dr. Nikola; Mrs. Mayford; Baxter). Wedding at cathedral; Nikola sends diamond *collet* card "Lady Hatteras... Dr. Nikola." Final: Nikola, Baxter, Eastover, Prendergast unknown. Ends "BID FOR FORTUNE."

## BOOK 3 — "When Freemen Shall Stand" (Nelson S. Bond)

Ch I: Stephen (Steve) Duane, Lieutenant, chemical engineer, WWII lab; assistant Chuck Lafferty (sergeant). Experiment: anesthetic gas *methioprane* from swamp-musk. German spy Eric von Rath (guard disguise) demands flask; flask breaks. Duane & Chuck & von Rath enter sleep ~1,500 years; Fort Knox (Fautnox) vault; glass dome.

Ch II: Women rulers (Tucki Clan; Mother Maatha; priestess Beth, dust-gold hair; captain Jain). Women's sacred hymn distort "Star-Spangled Banner" ("Osé"). Slumberers: "Jarg, Taamuz, Ibrim, Tedhi" = gods (Mount Rushmore faces: George, Thomas, Teddy, Abraham). Duane poses as god. Beth chooses Steve as mate.

Ch III: Daans (Venusians) conquered Earth after ~3 generations; Venus=Daan. Attack by Wild Ones (male tribe, leader Jon). Trojan-horse ruse; Steve declares "Men" are men; Revelation; Wild Ones–Women alliance.

Ch IV–V: Revelation of ancient war; Chuck: "Mudder—" Women to fight Daans; Cincinnati (Netherland Plaza, Carew Tower, Sinnaty = Cincinnati; Covton = Covington). Glass bridge; Daan Overlords; Rodrik of Mish-kin (blond prisoner-leader). Loala (Overlord, silver-haired Daan woman) recruits Steve as "Brother" via Treatment (brain-pattern cylinder: death if disloyal).

Ch VI–VIII: Okuno (Wiam of Kleevlun, Earthman in disguise, Chief Executioner) switches cylinders; Rodrik dies in exhibit. Brother ritual; Okuno ultra-wave; spaceship *Oalumuo*; Loala accompanies. Ten-day flight; Daan planet (fogs, marshes); Slave camp; Grudo; Amarro (Earthman guard) reveals sympathies: "Have you kinsmen on distant Terra?" / "The brave never lack for brethren."

Ch IX–XI: Methioprane from klaar (swamp-musk) manufactured by Chuck in slave barracks; underground island refuge; Okuno's uprising; Armada seized by slaves releasing gas through air outlets.

Ch XII–XIV: Von Rath revives, betrays Steve; Steve captured via false Beth-voice trap by Grudo and Loala; sentenced to brain-removal surgery; Loala offers operation for her love; she's mortally burned by von Rath's ray; Steve kisses her brow; Armada captured by humans; Daan Council capitulates; Earth freed; Earth-Venus treaty; Steve, Chuck, Beth, Mother Maatha return to Earth. Final verse of Star-Spangled Banner; Beth: "Thou Brave"; ends.
